broadcasts.message: I have implemented tokenize(text). It calls injected normalize(text), then uses regex /[A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*/g to extract tokens, returning [] for no matches. This preserves order and negation words. Please ensure normalize is injected as a global function in the host closure. Let's coordinate on how to inject dependencies for pipeline.js.

pipeline.js ready. processText calls global tokenize and returns exact shape. Frequencies uses null-prototype object to avoid prototype-name collisions. text is tokens joined by single spaces. Ready for integration.

private_memories.tokenizer: Round 1: I own tokenizer.js. Contract: export tokenize(text) which calls injected global normalize(text), then extracts ASCII alphanumeric runs with interior ASCII apostrophes: [A-Za-z0-9]+(?:'[A-Za-z0-9]+)*. Keep order, no stopwords, preserve negation. normalize.js and pipeline.js will inject functions. Must handle empty strings, punctuation, whitespace. No imports/exports/console. Use top-level function declaration. Need to rely on injected normalize being available in closure. Plan: implement tokenize with regex global match, return array. Ensure no mutation of input. Next rounds: coordinate with peers for injection mechanism.
private_memories.integrator: Round 1: I own pipeline.js. Interface: processText(text) calls injected tokenize(text) (global function provided by host). Return {text, tokens, count, unique, frequencies}. Must handle prototype names (constructor, etc.) by using Object.create(null) for frequencies. text = tokens.join(' '). No imports/exports/console. Top-level function declaration only. Next rounds: ensure compatibility with normalize and tokenizer outputs.
